commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: Let an action summary wrap, and adopt the new app icon
commits.body:
Buttons are `white-space: nowrap` globally, which is right for a label and wrong
for the three summary rows in a transcript: those hold a sentence. "Thought for
43s, read 1 file, wrote 1 file, edited 1 file, ran 2 commands" could not wrap, so
it ran past the row — measured at 395px inside a 341px column — and widened the
page with it, which moved the jump-to-top and jump-to-bottom buttons off the
right edge and cut off the composer and its send button.

The earlier attempt at this added `overflow-wrap` and `min-width` to the same
rows, which did nothing while `nowrap` was still in force. The inner span needs
its own `min-width` too, or the flex item keeps its full content width whatever
the parent says.

Four more full-width rows had the same inherited `nowrap` with nothing clipping
it — the model options, the command palette, menu items and the folder picker.
They list a name or a path, where one line each is the point, so they end in an
ellipsis rather than wrapping.

The icon is replaced everywhere it is used: the web and PWA icons, the Electron
packaging icon, and the source `@capacitor/assets` reads to build the Android
launcher set. Its background is a dark grey rather than the old navy, so the
adaptive icon's background colour follows it — left alone, the artwork would sit
on a field that does not match its own edges. Splash sources are added in the
same artwork so the launch screen stops showing the previous mark on white.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: Put the app icon on white
commits.body:
The artwork arrives as a monogram on grey, and installing that left a grey tile
in the launcher. Dropping the backdrop altogether is not an option either: the
wide neon glow is the design, and keyed out it survives as a smudge that reads as
dirt on any pale surface.

So the key is tight — chroma high enough to hold the letterforms and the bloom
right around them, with a luminance floor that drops the dark outer haze — and
what survives goes on white, in the launcher icon, the favicon and PWA set, the
Electron packaging icon, the Capacitor source the Android launcher set is built
from, and the splash. The adaptive icon's background colour follows, so the tile
is white rather than the artwork's original grey.

White also settles the header mark. The monogram's lower half is dark blue, which
all but vanished against the dark theme; a white tile reads on either one.

commits.subject: feat(i18n): add Simplified Chinese (zh-CN) translations (#120)
commits.body:
Add a complete zh-CN dictionary (all 290 keys, at full parity with English), a new language picker entry, and region-aware auto-detection so Simplified Chinese browsers no longer fall back to Traditional Chinese (zh/zh-Hans/zh-CN/zh-SG/zh-MY map to zh-CN; zh-Hant/zh-TW/zh-HK/zh-MO keep zh-TW).

Update the language lists in README and CONTRIBUTING.

Verified with the full CI suite: build, build:electron, test:i18n, test:config, test:ui, test:settings, test:model, test:events, test:profiles, test:desktop, and bridge tests all pass.

commits.author: Lucca Pinto
commits.subject: feat: attach images to a prompt on the OMP bridge (#121)
commits.body:
* feat(bridge): accept image attachments and forward them as ACP image blocks

* feat(web): attach images to a prompt from the composer

* docs: document image attachments in the OMP bridge section

* feat: keep an attached image visible when a session is reopened

OMP replays a stored image as an ACP image chunk and persists it in the session
transcript as { type: image, data, mimeType }, re-encoded to WebP and without the
original filename. Both replay paths now map that to a file part, and the app draws
file parts as bounded thumbnails, so an attachment no longer disappears from the
conversation the moment it is sent.

Image chunks are accepted only while replaying: OMP echoes a live prompt back, and
the bridge already recorded that attachment when it sent it.

* fix(web): gate the attachment control on the harness capability

The PR described the paperclip as hidden on harnesses that do not accept images, but
it rendered unconditionally: only /v1/capabilities knew, and it never reported the flag.
PI, Claude Code and Codex CLI therefore offered an attachment flow whose only possible
outcome was 'This harness does not accept images' at send time.

The bridge now derives 'attachments' from the agent's own initialize handshake rather
than the static profile table, so a harness that stops advertising images stops offering
the control, and the app gates the picker on it the way it already gates rename, delete,
models and todos. Staged attachments are dropped when the connection changes, since they
belong to the server they were staged on.

Verified against a real omp acp (attachments true, paperclip present) and against a
stub agent advertising no image capability (attachments false, paperclip and file input
absent from the DOM), at 420px and 1280px.

commits.author: joyfish666
commits.subject: fix(web): raise message and session action menus above the composer
commits.body:
The message context menu (long-press on a phone, right-click on desktop)
and the header session actions menu both hardcoded z-index: 20, tying them
to the --z-sticky layer the composer sits on. The composer stacks at the
same level and comes later in the DOM, so in both layouts — the mobile
bottom sheet and a desktop right-click menu near the composer — its top
items (Copy text / Copy Markdown) were covered by the input box and
taps/clicks landed on the composer instead of the menu.

Use the --z-menu token (30) so both menus stack above the composer and
every sticky element, matching the other dropdowns, and update the UI
regression assertion accordingly.
